# Weather, QBs, injuries, Kalshi {#sec-rounds45}

```{python}
exec(open("_common.py").read())
import json
r4 = json.loads((ROOT / "models" / "round4_weather_qb.json").read_text())
r5 = json.loads((ROOT / "models" / "round5_availability.json").read_text())
kb = json.loads((ROOT / "models" / "kalshi_backtest.json").read_text())
clv = json.loads((ROOT / "models" / "clv_history.json").read_text())
```

@sec-improvements ended with a diagnosis: the gap to the market is **information, not
modeling**. This chapter adds the information we could get for free and tests each piece
with the same pre-registered rule. Every candidate was written down and committed before
it was run (`docs/experiments/2026-09-24_*`).

## Does the market agree with us? Closing-line value

Before adding anything, a measurement. Closing-line value (CLV) is how far the line moves
toward a bet between the open (where we'd bet) and kickoff. A bettor whose lines keep
moving their way has information the market later adopts, even in weeks when results go
against them.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-clv
#| tbl-cap: "Closing-line value of the practice rules, out of sample 2021–2025 (points of line movement toward the bet)."
names = {"edge4 (model side, |edge| >= 4)": "Model 4+ points off the total",
         "shootout_under": "Under in shootouts", "all games, model side": "Every game, model's side"}
t = pd.DataFrame(clv["all"])
t["Rule"] = t.rule.map(names)
t["Seasons with CLV > 0"] = [sum(clv["by_season"][s][i]["avg CLV (pts)"] > 0 for s in clv["by_season"])
                             for i in range(len(t))]
t.rename(columns={"bets": "Bets", "avg CLV (pts)": "Avg CLV", "win % vs open": "Won vs open (%)"})[
    ["Rule", "Bets", "Avg CLV", "Won vs open (%)", "Seasons with CLV > 0"]].set_index("Rule")
```

The model's big disagreements with the opening total carry real information: the line
moves toward them in every season. The shootout under is a different animal: it wins,
but the line doesn't move toward it, a bias the market leaves in place all week.

## Round 4: weather and quarterbacks

Weather: wind, rain and temperature over the 3.5 hours from kickoff, from the nearest
weather station for past games (Meteostat) and the forecast for upcoming ones
(Open-Meteo). Quarterbacks: the team's most recent starter, his experience and passing
efficiency, and whether the starter just changed, from the passing box score.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-round4
#| tbl-cap: "Round 4 candidates. Decision seasons 2021–2023, check seasons 2024–2025."
t4 = pd.DataFrame(r4["table"])
d = t4[t4.period == "decide 2021-23"].set_index("candidate")
c = t4[t4.period == "check 2024-25"].set_index("candidate")
pd.DataFrame({"Total 21–23": d["total MAE"], "Margin 21–23": d["margin MAE"],
              "O/U 21–23": d["O/U open %"], "Total 24–25": c["total MAE"],
              "O/U 24–25": c["O/U open %"]}).round(2).rename_axis(None)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-round4-verdict
#| tbl-cap: "Round 4 verdicts (primary metric: total MAE for weather, margin MAE for quarterbacks)."
pd.DataFrame(r4["verdicts"]).T.rename(columns={"seasons better (of 3)": "Seasons better",
    "gain 95% CI": "Gain, 95% interval", "adopt": "Adopted", "metric": "Metric"})
```

Weather improves total-points error in all three decision seasons and was **adopted**. W2 (the same idea as thresholds) also passed, with a weaker interval; only the stronger version, W1, went into the model.
The gain is small, and it lowers the error more than it moves the O/U record, which goes
down in 2021–23 and up in 2024–25. Quarterback features add nothing the team ratings
don't already carry.

## Round 5: an injury proxy

No free source publishes college football injury reports as data. The closest thing is
the box score: a key player (the QB, top two rushers, top three receivers, top three
tacklers) who had stats earlier in the season but **none in his team's previous game**.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-round5
#| tbl-cap: "Round 5: key-player availability (primary metric: margin MAE)."
pd.DataFrame(r5["verdicts"]).T.rename(columns={"seasons better (of 3)": "Seasons better",
    "gain 95% CI": "Gain, 95% interval", "adopt": "Adopted", "metric": "Metric"})
```

Not adopted. Many of those players return the next week, and when they don't, the news
reaches the line before kickoff. The flag stays on the website as information.

## Kalshi: halves, quarters and team totals

Kalshi lists what our sportsbook data doesn't. Two findings came before any bet:

1. **Split the market, don't replace it.** Each team's points implied by the sportsbook
   line, split across halves and quarters by the model's shares, beat the period models
   in every period. The period models alone predicted medians, so their quarters summed
   to about 47 points against about 53 for the full game.
2. **Honest ladders.** The chance a period lands over any line comes from the model's
   out-of-sample errors; on 2024–2025 lines the calibration error is under 3.5 points.

Then the test that matters: real Kalshi prices from 2026 weeks 1–3, four hours before
kickoff, with the pre-registered rules.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-kalshi
#| tbl-cap: "Kalshi backtest, 2026 weeks 1–3 (profit after fees)."
tiers = {"best": "Best", "light": "Lean", "pass": "Everything else"}
rows = [{"Tier": tiers[k], "Bets": v["bets"], "Win %": v["win %"], "ROI %": v["ROI %"]}
        for k, v in kb["tiers"].items() if k in tiers]
p = kb["picks (best + lean)"]
rows.append({"Tier": "Best + Lean", "Bets": p["bets"], "Win %": p["win %"], "ROI %": p["ROI %"]})
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Tier")
```

On all `{python} kb["main_lines"]` main lines, Kalshi's own prices predicted outcomes
slightly better than the model (Brier `{python} kb["brier_kalshi_mid"]` vs
`{python} kb["brier_model"]`). Not adopted for picks: the site shows Kalshi prices next to
the model's chance as information, and the would-be picks are logged on paper so the 2026
season can settle it.

## Where that leaves us

The information that would close the gap (who is actually playing this week) isn't
available for free. What was available (weather) went in, and what didn't help was
documented and left out. The recommendations stay where the evidence is: totals, and
only when the win chance clears 54%.
